title: Dispatch OGF 6: Northern Families Leave as Reservoir Wall Opens
summary: The first visible crack follows the path of the glass roots.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A crack wide enough to admit a pencil appeared yesterday in the lower wall of the Northmere Reservoir. Water seeped through it before engineers closed the channel above. Inspector Voss ordered the remaining northern streets evacuated, moving the city’s preparations ahead of the hour shown in the fruit.

Miss Armitage and the children from the worker’s cottages left by noon. Mr. Fenner lent his cart to the wardens and carried bedding across the east bridge. By evening, North Loom Street was empty. From the boarding house window, Miss Morrow observed that it resembled the dry scene in Dr. Saye’s pear.

Not every scene has been averted. Fruit picked this morning showed a line of wagons on the bridge before they arrived. The city has instructed wardens to use tested roads and to disregard any route that appears safe only inside a pear.

Mrs. Rill has authorized removal of the mirrorwood graft. Dr. Saye’s measurements show that the root threads lose their clarity when a branch is cut, but do not die at once. Their course beneath the reservoir remains connected to a buried heartstock under the oldest tree.

The Institute and city engineers will remove the heartstock at dawn tomorrow. They must first brace the drainage channel so that glass roots disappearing from its mortar do not leave it hollow. Mrs. Rill asked to be present. “Peter planted this,” she said. “I am the one who should see what has grown.”
